channel.title: Biology of Leadership
channel.description: Research-based, practical articles on decision-making under pressure, regulation and leadership for executives and key roles. By Esther Michele Kazir.

item.title: Conflict of Interest in Leadership Decisions About People You Know
item.description: Conflict of interest shapes leadership decisions about people you know before you notice it. What research shows about affiliation bias, and why good intentions are not enough.

item.title: Ethical Leadership Starts Before the Decision
item.description: Ethical leadership is often decided in the small moments before the formal decision. What research says about fairness in decision making, and one question to ask the room.

item.title: Trust in Teams Is a Pattern, Not a Value: What Leaders Teach Under Pressure
item.description: Team trust is not built by values on the wall but by a pattern people learn to predict. What social decision-making research teaches leaders, and one question about the next piece of bad news.

item.title: Decision-Making Under Pressure: Urgency Does Not Remove Responsibility
item.description: Under pressure, a fast answer can feel like a clear one. What research says about emotion, stress and managerial decisions, plus a three-line check before you decide.

item.title: Responsibility Aversion: Why the Hardest Leadership Decision Is Not the Riskiest One
item.description: Research on responsibility aversion explains why leaders hesitate when a decision lands on others, and how to tell when a stalled decision needs ownership, not more data.
